x: From the start our new Member Wally Wortley ran extremely strongly, and in finishing so high up in such a distinguished field put up a really remarkable show.

Outstanding was the running of Wally Wortley who proved that not only has he got a formidable turn of speed but he can also stay well. Our runners ran most of the race as a pack and this undoubtedly helped in placing the team.

Wal Wortley showed a most welcome return to form and it was pleasing to see our late member Mick Porter, now of Manchester, in such good shape. we did however, suffer a severe misfortune when Bert Jordan retired with tendon trouble after 15 miles.
On 24th September three of our distance runners, W. Wortley, A, Bishop and J. McDonald, just sufficient for a team, set off on the long run to Brighton.
Wortley finished third in the Doncaster Marathon, to Leeds and Hull. An outstanding performance was achieved by R.
At the end of the first lap Collin Collis and Eric Gebbett were running with the leading bunch of men, with W. Wortley, A.
Wortley who had finished second last year.
It was good to see our London to Brighton men, Alan Bishop, MacDonald and Wortley sharpening up early in the season, it is hoped they will soon be starting their long preparation.

Discretion was the better part of valour and the old hands Wally Wortley, Alan Bishop, Geoff Pearson, Alf Byford, Arthur Penstone and John MacDonald were making certain that their race would last the full distance - good team stuff !
